Quality & Evidence-Based Practice

Quality improvement and evidence-based practice — audits, standards, EBP steps and nursing sensitive outcomes.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define quality improvement and evidence-based practice
  • List the steps of EBP
  • Describe nursing sensitive outcomes

In simple words

Quality improvement (QI) is the ongoing effort to make care safer, more effective and more patient-centred. Evidence-based practice (EBP) uses the best research evidence, clinical expertise and patient preferences to make decisions.

Together, QI and EBP improve patient outcomes.

Steps of EBP

Step What to do
Ask Form a clinical question (PICO)
Acquire Search for the best evidence
Appraise Critically appraise the evidence
Apply Integrate with expertise and patient preference
Assess Evaluate the outcome

Nursing sensitive outcomes

  • Patient falls.
  • Pressure ulcers.
  • Hospital-acquired infections.
  • Medication errors.
  • Patient satisfaction.

Quality improvement

  • Audits — check care against standards.
  • Standards — expected levels of care.
  • Indicators — measurable outcomes.
  • PDCA cycle — Plan, Do, Check, Act.

🔴 EBP combines three things

Evidence-based practice combines best research evidence, clinical expertise and patient preferences to make decisions.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Ask clinical questions — use PICO (Patient, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome).
  • Use best evidence — read guidelines and research before changing practice.
  • Join audits — help check care against standards.
  • Monitor outcomes — track falls, infections, medication errors on your ward.
  • Suggest improvements — use PDCA to test small changes.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Quality improvement makes care safer, more effective and more patient-centred.
  2. EBP combines research evidence, clinical expertise and patient preferences.
  3. EBP steps: Ask, Acquire, Appraise, Apply, Assess.
  4. Nursing sensitive outcomes: falls, pressure ulcers, infections, medication errors, satisfaction.
  5. QI tools: audits, standards, indicators, PDCA cycle.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. PICO forms a clinical question (Patient, Intervention, Comparison, Outcome).
  2. PDCA = Plan, Do, Check, Act — a cycle for testing improvements.
  3. Evidence-based practice improves patient outcomes.
  4. Nurses collect data and participate in quality projects.

📌 Memory trick

EBP 5 A’s: “Ask, Acquire, Appraise, Apply, Assess” — say it like “a-k-a-a-a”.

60-second revision

  • QI improves care safety, effectiveness, patient-centred care.
  • EBP = evidence + expertise + patient preferences.
  • Steps: Ask, Acquire, Appraise, Apply, Assess.
  • Nursing sensitive outcomes: falls, pressure ulcers, infections, med errors, satisfaction.
  • QI tools: audits, standards, indicators, PDCA.

Test yourself

EBP stands for:

Answer: A. EBP = Evidence-Based Practice.

The first step of EBP is:

Answer: B. Ask — form a clinical question (using PICO).

A nursing sensitive outcome is:

Answer: B. Patient falls are a nursing sensitive outcome.

PDCA stands for:

Answer: A. PDCA = Plan, Do, Check, Act.

Quality improvement aims to:

Answer: B. QI aims to make care safer, more effective and more patient-centred.
